wrong_idea: PED is the slope of the demand curve, so it is the same all along it
correction: Slope uses absolute changes; PED uses percentage changes, so it varies along a straight-line demand curve.

wrong_idea: Divide the change in price by the change in quantity.
correction: Quantity goes on top: % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price.

wrong_idea: An elastic good has a PED below 1, because demand hardly changes
correction: Ignoring the sign, elastic means greater than 1: quantity changes proportionally more than price.

wrong_idea: Supply is just as elastic in the short run as in the long run
correction: Supply is usually more elastic in the long run because firms can change all their inputs.

wrong_idea: PES is usually negative, just like PED for most goods
correction: PES is usually positive because a higher price leads firms to supply more.

wrong_idea: YED measures how demand responds to a change in the good's price
correction: YED uses the change in income; the good's own price is held constant.

wrong_idea: An indirect tax shifts the demand curve, because buyers now pay more
correction: The tax is paid by firms, so it raises their costs and shifts supply, not demand.

wrong_idea: Producers bear the tax, as they are the ones who hand it to the government
correction: Who hands the money over does not decide who bears it; the split depends on elasticities.

wrong_idea: A pollution tax set at the right level brings pollution down to zero
correction: A tax equal to the marginal external cost internalises the externality: output falls to the social optimum and the welfare loss goes, but the efficient amount of pollution, usually above zero, remains.

wrong_idea: Work out the percentage changes from the new values.
correction: Percentage changes are worked out from the original values: change divided by original, times 100.

wrong_idea: PED is the change in quantity divided by the change in price, with no percentages.
correction: Absolute changes depend on the units used; PED divides percentage changes, so it has no units.

wrong_idea: PED measures how much the price changes when demand changes.
correction: It is the other way round: PED measures how quantity demanded responds to a change in price.

wrong_idea: PES is the % change in price divided by the % change in quantity supplied
correction: Quantity goes on top: % change in quantity supplied divided by % change in price.

wrong_idea: Supply is price elastic when buyers have lots of substitutes to switch to
correction: Substitutes affect PED; PES depends on how easily firms can raise output (spare capacity, stocks and time).

wrong_idea: A necessity like bread has a negative income elasticity of demand
correction: Necessities are normal goods with YED between 0 and 1; only inferior goods have a negative YED.

wrong_idea: An ad valorem tax shifts supply by the same amount at every price
correction: An ad valorem tax is a percentage of the price, so the gap between the curves widens as price rises.

wrong_idea: The more price inelastic demand is, the more of the tax producers bear
correction: It is the other way round: buyers who can't cut back end up paying more of the tax through a higher price.

wrong_idea: Firms just pay a pollution tax and carry on, so output does not change
correction: The tax makes polluting costlier, so firms cut pollution or output wherever that is cheaper than paying.

wrong_idea: A tax on pollution shifts demand, while a tax on the product shifts supply
correction: Both are paid by producers and raise their costs, so both shift supply; neither shifts demand.
